MinerU章节组块：32题双评对照

107块章节版重新答题32题，有效评分63/64。原117块版、PyMuPDF 81块版的回答与评分保留归档对照。

仅改变入库前的章节标签与分组；单篇论文、单轮回答。章节标签是程序推断元数据，原文保留。不同指标不相加为整体正确率，缺失评分不记零分。

结果解读与具体案例

  • 章节识别与组块已完成，但本轮没有得到两位裁判一致的质量提升。相对原117块，Luna的要点均分下降，Jev在30题配对集合上上升；事实和引用维度也存在裁判差异。
  • 对比当前PyMuPDF结构版时，新版在两位裁判各自相同题目上的要点得分、边界分和五项同时达标数均较低，默认索引继续保留PyMuPDF。
  • 第4、24、25题的要点评分在两位裁判下均比原117块版提高：分别补充了打浆作用力差异、贡献排名限制、补充表数值不可得的说明。
  • 第11题的新上下文没有包含70.42%到72.54%的数值反例；原117块上下文有这些数据。因此仍需改善关键表格召回，章节标签尚未保证找到对应结果小节。
  • 第28题新版只总结了PFI论文，没有说明第二篇论文未入库、无法比较，两位裁判均给该题必答要点0分。它因旧Jev评分缺失被排除在原117块的Jev主配对表外，不能忽略此退步。
  • 第32题新版遗漏摘要与正文相关系数不一致的说明，两位裁判都降低该项要点分；需要覆盖不同章节中的相关证据。
  • 第10题两版都列出了4.5至4.7 nm的数值序列，Jev两版要点均满分，Luna只给新版部分分。该差异应保留为评委尺度或表达完整性分歧，不全部归因于检索。
  • 下一轮优先诊断表格/跨章节证据覆盖与回答是否完成全部子问题；本轮未继续叠加优化，未根据评分改写已保存答案。

    "ref": "[2]",
    "page_start": 2,

    "text": "2. Methods\n\n2.1. PFI Refining\n\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets",

    "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

    "page_start": 2,
    "page_end": 2,
    "text": "2. Methods\n\n2.1. PFI Refining\n\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets",

    "ref": "[1]",
    "page_start": 2,
    "page_end": 2,
    "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

    "text": "2. Methods\n\n2.1. PFI Refining\n\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n2.2.   {
    "ref": "[1]",
    "page_start": 2,
    "page_end": 2,
    "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

The drainability was\ncharacterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Corresponding various pulps with an\nincreasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79◦SR, were obtained for softwood ﬁbers and 0,\n26, 40, 57, and 70◦SR were obtained for hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\nThe ﬁnes content, weighted mean length, and macro-ﬁbrillation index of each sample were\ndetermined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of\ndry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT\n12914-2008, respectively. PFI2-004 · PFI打到12000转的时候，针叶木浆和阔叶木浆的打浆度各是多少？那我们以后想要63 °SR左右的浆，是不是直接打12000转就行了？

参考答案与必答要点
方法部分给出的12000转对应针叶木63 °SR、阔叶木57 °SR。相同转数在本文不同浆种/条件下得到的打浆度不同，不能据此建立适用于所有纸浆的唯一换算。两类浆的作用力也不同，不能把差异全部归因于浆种。

在该文的PFI打浆条件下，针叶木浆在12000转时的打浆度为63 °SR。 [1]
同样在12000转时，阔叶木浆的打浆度为57 °SR。 [1]
因此，想要63 °SR左右的浆不能仅凭12000转直接套用；该转数只与针叶木浆的63 °SR相对应，而阔叶木浆在12000转约为57 °SR，且打浆度还取决于浆种和具体PFI条件，需实际试打并检测。 [1]

  {
    "ref": "[1]",
    "page_start": 2,
    "page_end": 2,
    "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

PyMuPDF结构81块

在PFI打到12000转时，针叶木浆的打浆度为63 °SR。 [1]
在同一研究中，阔叶木浆在12000转时的打浆度为57 °SR。 [1]
该研究将0、4000、8000、12000、16000转依次对应为针叶木浆16、20、40、63、79 °SR，以及阔叶木浆0、26、40、57、70 °SR。 [1]
因此，要达到约63 °SR不能只依据固定12000转，因为该转数下两种浆的打浆度并不相同。 [1]
研究中针叶木和阔叶木的PFI每杆长作用力分别为3.33 N/mm和1.77 N/mm，表明两种浆的打浆条件并不相同。 [1]

    "text": "2. Methods\n\n2.1. PFI Reﬁning\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp ﬁbers were obtained from\nZhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI reﬁner\n(Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency\nof 10%, the gap between the opposite reﬁning plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were\n3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. The drainability was\ncharacterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp\nﬁbers were separately reﬁned in a PFI reﬁner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and\nat 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an\nincreasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79◦SR, were obtained for softwood ﬁbers and 0,\n26, 40, 57, and 70◦SR were obtained for hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\nThe ﬁnes content, weighted mean length, and macro-ﬁbrillation index of each sample were\ndetermined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of\ndry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT\n12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus\n(Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. MinerU原生117块

WRV采用0.5 g（o.d.）样品并按照ISO 23714测定。 [1]
WRV的计算公式为 WRV(%)=((m1−m2)/m2)×100%。 [1]
公式中 m1 是离心后样品的质量，m2 是烘干后样品的质量。 [1]

    "text": "2.3. Water Retention Value (WRV)\n\nThe WRV was determined with 0.5 g samples (o.d.) according to ISO 23714.\n\n$$\nW R V(\\%) = \\frac{(m_ {1} - m_ {2})}{m_ {2}}\\times 100\\%\\tag{1}\n$$\n\nwhere $m _ { 1 }$ is the weight of the sample after centrifugation and $m _ { 2 }$ is the weight of the oven-dried sample.\n\n2.4. XRD Analysis\n\nThe crystallinity of pretreated fibers was determined by a Shimadzu XRD 7000S (Shimadzu, Kyoto, Japan), while using Cu-Ka radiation. The samples were scanned at 40 kV and 30 mA in a 2θ range of $4 { - } 4 0 ^ { \\circ }$ at 1<sup>◦</sup>/min. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in native cellulose; for clarity, all of the reflections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis, the experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The two types of CI values were obtained from peak intensity method (CI − XI) and peak fitting (CI-XA), respectively. The CI − XI was calculated as in Equation (2) [19].",

XRD Analysis\nThe crystallinity of pretreated ﬁbers was determined by a Shimadzu XRD 7000S (Shimadzu,\nKyoto, Japan), while using Cu-Ka radiation. The samples were scanned at 40 kV and 30 mA in a 2θ\nrange of 4–40◦at 1◦/min. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in\nnative cellulose; for clarity, all of the reﬂections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis,\nthe experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The two types of CI\nvalues were obtained from peak intensity method (CI −XI) and peak ﬁtting (CI-XA), respectively.\nThe CI −XI was calculated as in Equation (2) [19].\n(I200 −Iam) CI −XI = × 100% (2)\nI200\nwhere I200 is the maximum diﬀraction intensity value of the (200) lattice plane between the scattering\nangles of 2θ = 22◦and 23◦, and Iam is the minimum diﬀraction intensity of amorphous fraction between\n2θ = 18◦and 19◦.\nAll of the XRD diﬀractograms were smoothed with the Savitzky–Golay algorithm and\nbaseline-corrected with linear ﬁt function. Subsequently, the baseline-corrected diﬀractograms\nwere deconvoluted with the Pearson VII function. The value of the CI-XA equals the area percentage\noccupied by crystalline peaks over the total area of the diﬀraction pattern [20]. In addition, the crystallite\nsize was calculated by the widely used Scherrer Equation (3) [21]:\nk × λ\nL = (3)\n(β × cos θ)\nwhere L is the size that is perpendicular to the lattice plane, k is a constant that depends on the crystal\nshape (0.89), λ is the wavelength of the incident beam in the diﬀraction experiment (0.154 nm), β is the\nfull width at half maximum of the diﬀraction peak, and θ is the Bragg’s angle. In general, the values of\nthe calculated crystallite sizes might be lower than that of the real crystallite sizes, because the peak\nbroadening from the instrumental factors was not considered [22].\n\n2.5. FT-IR Analysis\nTHE FT-IR spectra were recorded on solid samples in KBr pellets by means of an FT-IR Bruker\nVertex 70 spectrometer (Karlsruhe, Germany). Unreﬁned and reﬁned ﬁbers were smashed into powder\nbetween 40 and 60 mesh. Subsequently, the powder sample of each species (5 mg) was dispersed in a\nmatrix of highly pure KBr (500 mg). The spectral was recorded by averaging 64 recordings and at a\nresolution of 4 cm−1 with transmission mode from 4000 cm−1 to 400 cm−1. PFI2-007 · CI-XI与CI-XA有什么区别？请给出本文CI-XI的公式，并说明CI-XA依据什么计算。

参考答案与必答要点
CI-XI用衍射峰强度计算：(I200−Iam)/I200×100%。CI-XA用晶区峰面积占总衍射面积的百分比计算，来自峰拟合。两者采用不同口径。

MinerU原生117块

CI-XI和CI-XA是两种结晶度指数：前者采用峰强度法获得，后者采用峰拟合/峰面积法获得。 [3]
CI-XI值来自衍射强度之比，而CI-XA值来自峰面积之比。 [1]
本文CI-XI的计算公式为 CI-XI = ((I200 − Iam)/I200) × 100%；其中 I200 是 2Θ=22°–23° 之间(200)晶面的最大衍射强度，Iam 是 2Θ=18°–19° 之间无定形部分的最小衍射强度。 [3]
CI-XA依据峰拟合后的面积计算：其值等于结晶峰面积占整个衍射图谱总面积的百分比。 [3]
进行CI-XA分析前，衍射图经Savitzky–Golay平滑和线性基线校正，然后用Pearson VII函数对基线校正后的衍射图进行解卷积。 [3]
本文中CI-XI的值显著高于CI-XA，可能归因于CI-XA分析中对无定形贡献的过拟合。 [2]

The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in native cellulose; for clarity, all of the reflections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis, the experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The two types of CI values were obtained from peak intensity method (CI − XI) and peak fitting (CI-XA), respectively. The CI − XI was calculated as in Equation (2) [19].\n\n$$\nC I - X I = \\frac {\\left(I _ {2 0 0} - I _ {a m}\\right)}{I _ {2 0 0}} \\times 1 0 0 \\%\\tag{2}\n$$\n\nwhere I200 is the maximum difraction intensity value of the (200) lattice plane between the scattering angles of $2 \\Theta = 2 2 ^ { \\circ }$ and $2 3 ^ { \\circ }$ , and $I _ { a m }$ is the minimum difraction intensity of amorphous fraction between $2 \\Theta = 1 8 ^ { \\circ }$ and $1 9 ^ { \\circ }$\n\nAll of the XRD difractograms were smoothed with the Savitzky–Golay algorithm and baseline-corrected with linear fit function. Subsequently, the baseline-corrected difractograms were deconvoluted with the Pearson VII function. The value of the CI-XA equals the area percentage occupied by crystalline peaks over the total area of the difraction pattern [20]. CI-XI与CI-XA都是XRD结晶度指数，但CI-XI基于XRD峰强度，CI-XA基于XRD峰面积。 [1] [3]
本文中CI-XI由峰强度法得到，CI-XA由峰拟合法得到。 [3]
CI-XI的计算公式为CI-XI=(I200−Iam)/I200×100%。 [3]
式中I200是2θ=22°–23°之间(200)晶面的最大衍射强度，Iam是2θ=18°–19°之间非晶部分的最小衍射强度。 [3]
CI-XA等于结晶峰面积占整个衍射图总面积的百分比。 [3]
计算CI-XA时，先对基线校正后的衍射图用Pearson VII函数去卷积；CI-XA可理解为基于峰面积。 [1] [3]

PyMuPDF结构81块

本文中CI-XI由峰强度法获得，CI-XA由峰拟合获得。 [3]
本文CI-XI的公式为 CI-XI = (I200 − Iam) / I200 × 100%。 [3]
式中I200为2θ=22°–23°之间(200)晶面的最大衍射强度，Iam为2θ=18°–19°之间无定形部分的最小衍射强度。 [3]
CI-XA等于结晶峰面积占整个衍射图总面积的百分比。 [3]
CI-XA是在Savitzky–Golay平滑和线性基线校正后，用Pearson VII函数对基线校正后的衍射图进行解卷积后计算的。 [3]
CI-XI的值明显高于CI-XA，这可能是因为CI-XA分析中对无定形贡献的过度拟合。 [2]
CI-XI与CI-XA仍显著相关，软木纤维的相关系数为0.919（p < 0.05），硬木纤维为0.925（p < 0.05）。 [2]

luna：要点100.00%；事实7/7；引用7/7；引用组7/7；边界2/2。

    "text": "Figure 4. The CI-XI (crystallinity index obtained by comparing intensity of X-ray difractometer (XRD) peaks) and CI-XA (crystallinity index obtained by comparing area of XRD peaks) for refined and unrefined samples: (a) softwood fiber and (b) hardwood fiber.\n\nTable 1. (a) The CI of softwood fibers through refining. (b) The CI of hardwood fibers through refining.\n\n<sup>a</sup> The CI-XI value was obtained from the ratio of the difraction intensity. <sup>b</sup> The CI-XA value was obtained from the ratio of the peak areas.\n\n<table><tr><td colspan=\"6\">(a)</td></tr><tr><td rowspan=\"2\">Revolutions</td><td colspan=\"2\">CI (%)</td><td colspan=\"3\">Crystallite Size (nm)</td></tr><tr><td> $CI-XI^a$ </td><td> $CI-XA^b$ </td><td>110</td><td>(110)</td><td>(200)</td></tr><tr><td>0</td><td>73.23</td><td>40.46</td><td>3.2</td><td>3.5</td><td>4.5</td></tr><tr><td>4000</td><td>70.42</td><td>37.71</td><td>3.1</td><td>3.4</td><td>4.6</td></tr><tr><td>8000</td><td>72.54</td><td>39.65</td><td>3.2</td><td>3.4</td><td>4.6</td></tr><tr><td>12,000</td><td>70.93</td><td>36.22</td><td>3.1</td><td>3.7</td><td>4.7</td></tr><tr><td>16,000</td><td>69.82</td><td>34.20</td><td>3.2</td><td>3.5</td><td>4.7</td></tr><tr><td></td><td colspan=\"5\">(b)</td></tr><tr><td rowspan=\"2\">Revolutions</td><td colspan=\"2\">CI (%)</td><td colspan=\"3\">Crystallite Size (nm)</td></tr><tr><td> $CI-XI^a$ </td><td> $CI-XA^b$ </td><td>110</td><td>(110)</td><td>(200)</td></tr><tr><td>0</td><td>75.55</td><td>47.16</td><td>3.1</td><td>3.1</td><td>4.5</td></tr><tr><td>4000</td><td>73.01</td><td>36.26</td><td>3.1</td><td>3.3</td><td>4.7</td></tr><tr><td>8000</td><td>75.06</td><td>42.35</td><td>3.1</td><td>3.5</td><td>4.8</td></tr><tr><td>12,000</td><td>74.57</td><td>39.21</td><td>2.9</td><td>4.0</td><td>4.8</td></tr><tr><td>16,000</td><td>73.55</td><td>38.01</td><td>3.0</td><td>3.7</td><td>4.7</td></tr></table>\n\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury",

Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. PFI2-011 · 是不是打浆转数越高，纤维素结晶度就越低？

参考答案与必答要点
不是单调下降。针叶木CI-XI从4000转70.42%升到8000转72.54%；阔叶木也从73.01%升到75.06%。0转到16000转总体下降，但过程中先降、回升、再降。

MinerU原生117块

PFI精磨对纤维素结晶度的影响存在不同结论：有研究报道结晶度下降，也有研究报道随精磨程度先升高后降低或波动，尚未识别出明确趋势。 [1]
本研究中软木浆和硬木浆的CI-XI与CI-XA在0、4000、8000、12000、16000转下并非随转数单调降低，而是出现下降后回升等波动。 [7]
总体而言，PFI精磨过程中微晶尺寸、结晶度和各种氢键含量变化不大。 [5]
研究还发现，PFI精磨过程中CI-XI与O(6)H···O(3')分子间氢键含量呈显著正相关。 [5]
因此，不能仅根据打浆转数升高直接推断纤维素结晶度必然降低，而需考虑具体浆种和精磨阶段。 [1] [7]

    "text": "1. Introduction\n\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

MinerU章节107块

关于PFI打浆对纤维素结晶度的影响，现有研究结论并不一致：有研究报道结晶度下降，也有研究报道结晶度先升高后下降，或出现波动，未识别出明确趋势。 [1]
该研究结论指出，在PFI refining过程中，微晶尺寸、结晶度和各类氢键含量总体变化不大，可认为PFI refining对超分子结构的破坏相对较小。 [6]
因此，不能简单断言打浆转数越高结晶度就越低；转数升高与结晶度降低之间并非普遍、必然的单调关系。 [1] [6]

    "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

不能简单认为打浆转数越高结晶度就越低；关于PFI打浆对纤维素结晶度的影响，文献结论并不一致。 [3]
有研究报道结晶度随打浆程度先升后降，或先波动上升再下降并重复波动，且此前研究未识别出明确趋势。 [4]
本研究中软木与硬木纤维的CI随PFI转数呈波动变化而非单调下降，例如软木CI-XI在0、4000、8000、12000、16000 r分别为73.23%、70.42%、72.54%、70.93%、69.82%。 [5]
总体而言，该研究认为PFI打浆过程中晶粒尺寸、结晶度和各类氢键含量总体变化不大，PFI打浆对超分子结构破坏相对较小。 [1]

    "text": "Keywords: natural cellulosic ﬁbers; mechanical reﬁning; Crystallinity; Crystallite size;\nHydrogen bonds\n\n1. Introduction\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired\nphysical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic ﬁbers. Therein,\nPapirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning is the most common laboratory reﬁner in order to\nimprove the inter-ﬁber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-ﬁbrillated\nor nano-ﬁbrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on ﬁbers are: (i) internal\nﬁbrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of ﬁber wall; (ii) external ﬁbrillation—peeling of\nﬁbrils from the ﬁber surface while remaining attached; (iii) ﬁber shortening—ﬁber cutting due to\nshearing action, and (iv) ﬁnes formation—primary ﬁnes come from ray cells and parenchyma cells\nand microﬁbrils that are caused by ﬁber shortening or external ﬁbrillation. Moreover, the PFI reﬁning\ncould be adopted to obtain a higher internal ﬁbrillation than other laboratory reﬁners [1]. These eﬀects\nof the PFI reﬁning on cellulosic ﬁbers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the ﬂexibility, and the\ninter-ﬁber bonding capacity of ﬁbers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and\nproperties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during reﬁning [7,8].\n\nThere are some diﬀerent conclusions regarding to the eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on crystallinity of\ncellulose, not like that of ball milling, which eﬀectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment\nprogresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI reﬁning\nfor corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased\nPolymers 2020, 12, 2912; doi:10.3390/polym12122912 www.mdpi.com/journal/polymers",

MinerU原生117块

PFI打浆过程中，软木纤维和硬木纤维的CI-XI与CI-XA均呈现相似趋势，即先下降、再上升，随后再次下降。 [1]
这种结晶度波动可能源于PFI打浆的机械作用作用于纤维素的不同区域。 [1]
在第一打浆阶段，CI下降表明机械处理可能主要作用于结晶区。 [1]
随后CI上升可解释为更大的作用力作用于无定形区，并在PFI打浆的机械与热作用下的干燥过程中可能发生共结晶（cocrystallization）。 [1]
之后的CI下降则可能是由于结晶区被持续破坏。 [1]

MinerU章节107块

在PFI打浆中，软木纤维和硬木纤维的CI-XI与CI-XA均呈现先下降、再上升、随后下降的相似趋势。 [2]
第一打浆阶段CI下降，表明机械处理可能主要作用于结晶区。 [2]
随后CI上升，可解释为在PFI打浆的机械和热作用下，非晶区受到更大作用并在干燥时可能发生共结晶。 [2]
之后的CI下降可能源于结晶区被持续破坏。 [2]
CI的波动被认为是因为PFI打浆的机械作用作用于纤维素的不同区域。 [2]

PyMuPDF 81块归档对照

PyMuPDF结构81块

PFI打浆过程中结晶度先下降，是因为初始打浆阶段机械处理主要作用于结晶区。 [3]
随后结晶度上升，可解释为更大的作用力作用于无定形区，干燥时在PFI打浆的机械和热作用下可能发生共结晶。 [3]
之后结晶度再次下降，可能是结晶区被持续破坏。 [3]
因此结晶度的波动可能源于PFI打浆机械作用作用于纤维素的不同区域。 [3]
O(6)H···O(3′)氢键含量与CI-XI呈相似变化，且结晶区中该氢键含量高于无定形区。 [6]

    "text": "In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood ﬁber, the trend of content\ncan be described as two phases. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood ﬁber, it increased\nﬁrstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both ﬁbers, the content of\nO(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of reﬁning from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to\nthe fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than\nO(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend\nin general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the\nbreakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and\nhigher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose\nmore accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber,\nthe number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions\nincreasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to\n12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups,\nwhich makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although\nthere is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6)\nmight disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase\nupon drying.\n\n3.4. 随着PFI打浆转数增加，打浆度和WRV均显著提高。 [1]
作者解释，这是因为更高程度的纤维化产生了新的表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
PFI打浆的主要作用包括内部纤维化，即纤维壁的分层、松散和润胀，以及外部纤维化等，这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [2]
纤维素分子间氢键断裂会导致更广泛的分层和更高的比表面积，使纤维素更易接触水和化学试剂。 [5]
WRV表征的润胀增加使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]

    "text": "1. Introduction\n\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

      "status": "needs_source_review",
      "exact_other_pages": [],

    }

    "text": "As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.\n\n3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds decreased first and then had an increase, followed by a decline for the two fibers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation coeficients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 $( p < 0 . 0 5 )$ for hardwood fibers, respectively. The similar trends in the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a higher content of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated in Figure 9 [35].",

MinerU章节107块

随着PFI打浆转数增加，打浆度和WRV均显著升高。 [1]
作者解释这种升高是由更高程度的fibrillation造成的，因为它产生了新的表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
以WRV表征的润胀增加使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
PFI打浆的主要作用包括内部fibrillation，即纤维壁的分层、松散和润胀，并提高纤维的可及性、润胀、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [2]

Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\nFor softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers, the macro-ﬁbrillation index and the ﬁber length had\na downward trend, and the ﬁnes content has an upward trend for the softwood ﬁbers during PFI\nreﬁning, as can be seen in Figure 1. The macro-ﬁbrillation index and ﬁber length of softwood ﬁbers\nchanged signiﬁcantly. However, two parameters of hardwood ﬁbers had no signiﬁcant variations\nrelative to softwood ﬁbers. It might be because of the lower reﬁning pressure that was applied in\nhardwood ﬁbers. The macro-ﬁbrillation index characterizes external macro-ﬁbrillation. The results of\nﬁber morphology analysis showed that external ﬁbrillation increased with the reﬁning process. It is\nconsistent with the increasing speciﬁc surface area (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource).\n\nFigure 1. The morphological analysis for the unreﬁned and reﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁbers and\n(b) hardwood ﬁbers.\nThe beating degree and the WRV had a signiﬁcant increment with increasing PFI reﬁning\nrevolutions, as can be seen in Figure 2. It is caused by the higher ﬁbrillation that produces the\nnew surface and more pores (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource). The increase in swelling\ncharacterized by WRV makes the ﬁbers more compliant in transverse [1], which contributes to\nimproving the inter-ﬁber bonding strength of the ﬁber network.     "text": "polymers\nArticle\nProbing Eﬀect of Papirindustriens Forskningsinstitut\n(PFI) Reﬁning on Aggregation Structure of Cellulose:\nCrystal Packing and Hydrogen-Bonding Network\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao * and Beihai He\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd.,\nTianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.)\n* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that aﬀects the properties of cellulosic\nﬁbers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning on the\nmolecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between\nthe crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic ﬁbers. The results showed that\nthe polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost\nunchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed\nwith reﬁning. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds was signiﬁcantly\ncorrelated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson\ncorrelation coeﬃcient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood ﬁbers and 0.889 (p < 0.05)\nfor hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling,\nand ﬁbrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds\nplay an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\nKeywords: natural cellulosic ﬁbers; mechanical reﬁning; Crystallinity; Crystallite size;\nHydrogen bonds\n\n1. Introduction\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired\nphysical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic ﬁbers. Therein,\nPapirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning is the most common laboratory reﬁner in order to\nimprove the inter-ﬁber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-ﬁbrillated\nor nano-ﬁbrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on ﬁbers are: (i) internal\nﬁbrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of ﬁber wall; (ii) external ﬁbrillation—peeling of\nﬁbrils from the ﬁber surface while remaining attached; (iii) ﬁber shortening—ﬁber cutting due to\nshearing action, and (iv) ﬁnes formation—primary ﬁnes come from ray cells and parenchyma cells\nand microﬁbrils that are caused by ﬁber shortening or external ﬁbrillation. Moreover, the PFI reﬁning\ncould be adopted to obtain a higher internal ﬁbrillation than other laboratory reﬁners [1]. These eﬀects\nof the PFI reﬁning on cellulosic ﬁbers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the ﬂexibility, and the\ninter-ﬁber bonding capacity of ﬁbers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and\nproperties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during reﬁning [7,8].\n\nThere are some diﬀerent conclusions regarding to the eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on crystallinity of\ncellulose, not like that of ball milling, which eﬀectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment\nprogresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI reﬁning\nfor corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased\nPolymers 2020, 12, 2912; doi:10.3390/polym12122912 www.mdpi.com/journal/polymers",

MinerU原生117块

针叶木和阔叶木打浆后纤维长度均呈下降趋势。 [2]
针叶木的纤维长度变化显著，而阔叶木的宏观纤维化指数和纤维长度相对针叶木无显著变化。 [2]
这种差别可能是因为阔叶木打浆时施加的 refining pressure 较低。 [2]
实验条件中针叶木和阔叶木的单位刀长作用力分别为 3.33 N/mm 和 1.77 N/mm。 [3]

针叶木经PFI打浆后纤维长度呈下降趋势，且纤维长度变化显著。 [2]
阔叶木经PFI打浆后纤维长度虽也呈下降趋势，但相对于针叶木无显著变化。 [2]
这种差别可能与阔叶木打浆时施加的打浆压力较低有关。 [2]
方法中针叶木和阔叶木的每杆长作用力分别为3.33 N/mm和1.77 N/mm，表明阔叶木受到的作用力较低。 [3]

        "text": "For softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, the macro-fibrillation index and the fiber length had a downward trend, and the fines content has an upward trend for the softwood fibers during PFI refining, as can be seen in Figure 1.     "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

针叶木和阔叶木在PFI打浆后纤维长度总体均呈下降趋势，但两者变化并不相同。 [1]
针叶木纤维长度变化显著，而阔叶木纤维长度没有相对针叶木那样的显著变化。 [1]

文中PFI打浆条件给出每齿长作用力为针叶木3.33 N/mm、阔叶木1.77 N/mm。 [7]

    "text": "3. Results and Discussions\n\n3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\nFor softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers, the macro-ﬁbrillation index and the ﬁber length had\na downward trend, and the ﬁnes content has an upward trend for the softwood ﬁbers during PFI\nreﬁning, as can be seen in Figure 1. The macro-ﬁbrillation index and ﬁber length of softwood ﬁbers\nchanged signiﬁcantly. However, two parameters of hardwood ﬁbers had no signiﬁcant variations\nrelative to softwood ﬁbers. It might be because of the lower reﬁning pressure that was applied in\nhardwood ﬁbers. The macro-ﬁbrillation index characterizes external macro-ﬁbrillation. The results of\nﬁber morphology analysis showed that external ﬁbrillation increased with the reﬁning process. It is\nconsistent with the increasing speciﬁc surface area (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource).\n\nFigure 1. The morphological analysis for the unreﬁned and reﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁbers and\n(b) hardwood ﬁbers.\nThe beating degree and the WRV had a signiﬁcant increment with increasing PFI reﬁning\nrevolutions, as can be seen in Figure 2. It is caused by the higher ﬁbrillation that produces the\nnew surface and more pores (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource). The increase in swelling\ncharacterized by WRV makes the ﬁbers more compliant in transverse [1], which contributes to\nimproving the inter-ﬁber bonding strength of the ﬁber network. The results of ﬁber morphology\nanalysis and water retention value showing that the ﬁbrillation and the separation between ﬁbrils\nincrease with the reﬁning process.",

    "text": "2. Methods\n\n2.1. PFI Reﬁning\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp ﬁbers were obtained from\nZhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI reﬁner\n(Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency\nof 10%, the gap between the opposite reﬁning plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were\n3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. The drainability was\ncharacterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp\nﬁbers were separately reﬁned in a PFI reﬁner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and\nat 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an\nincreasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79◦SR, were obtained for softwood ﬁbers and 0,\n26, 40, 57, and 70◦SR were obtained for hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\nThe ﬁnes content, weighted mean length, and macro-ﬁbrillation index of each sample were\ndetermined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of\ndry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT\n12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus\n(Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

PFI2-016 · 为什么本文认为纸张抗张性能提高，并不意味着单根纤维本身的强度也一定提高？零距抗张在这里有什么用？

参考答案与必答要点
作者将纸张抗张性能改善主要联系到细纤维化、细小纤维及纤维间结合。零距抗张指数用于表征纤维本身的抗张强度，结果表明本文PFI处理没有降低纤维强度。因此应区分纸页网络性能和纤维本身强度，不能只凭纸张变强推断单根纤维必然变强。

MinerU原生117块

本文把纸张抗张指数的提高主要归因于PFI精磨过程中的细纤维化和细小纤维增加，而不是单根纤维强度本身提高。 [1]
零距抗张指数通常用于表征纤维的拉伸强度。 [1]
零距抗张结果显示，PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度，这与Kouko等的报道一致。 [1]
精磨可提高纤维润胀、细纤维化和纸页抗张强度，同时在零距抗张上不出现纤维强度下降；因此纸页抗张提高不能据此推出单根纤维强度一定提高。 [1]

  "claim_assessments": [
    {
      "id": "C1",
      "text": "本文把纸张抗张指数的提高主要归因于PFI精磨过程中的细纤维化和细小纤维增加，而不是单根纤维强度本身提高。",
      "claim_type": "fact",
      "support": "partially_supported",
      "basis_locator": "E14",
      "basis": {
        "type": "reference_evidence",
        "text": "In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers."
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "C2",
      "text": "零距抗张指数通常用于表征纤维的拉伸强度。",
      "claim_type": "fact",
      "support": "supported",
      "basis_locator": "E14",
      "basis": {
        "type": "reference_evidence",
        "text": "In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers."
      }

纸张抗张强度的增量主要由PFI精磨过程中的细纤维化和细组分引起。 [1]
WRV表征的溶胀增加使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [2]
零距抗张指数通常用于表征纤维的抗张强度。 [1]
零距抗张结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度。 [1]
上述结果表明PFI精磨提高了纸张的抗张强度，同时没有降低纤维的抗张强度。 [1]

      "text": "WRV表征的溶胀增加使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。",
      "claim_type": "fact",
      "support": "supported",
      "basis_locator": "E13",
      "basis": {
        "type": "reference_evidence",
        "text": "The beating degree and the WRV had a significant increment with increasing PFI refining revolutions, as can be seen in Figure 2. It is caused by the higher fibrillation that produces the new surface and more pores (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource). The increase in swelling characterized by WRV makes the fibers more compliant in transverse [1], which contributes to improving the inter-fiber bonding strength of the fiber network.       }

      "basis_locator": "E14",
      "basis": {
        "type": "reference_evidence",
        "text": "In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. PyMuPDF结构81块

本文认为纸张抗张强度的提高主要来自PFI精磨过程中不断增强的细纤维化和细组分（fines）。 [1]
零距抗张指数通常用于表征纤维本身的抗张强度。 [1]
零距抗张结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度，这与Kouko等的报道一致。 [1]
因此，PFI精磨提高了细纤维化、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，同时未出现纤维抗张强度下降，但这不等同于单根纤维强度一定提高。 [1]

        "text": "In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above.     {
      "id": "C1",
      "text": "与阔叶木浆相比，针叶木浆的湿纸幅强度增幅更明显。",
      "claim_type": "fact",
      "support": "supported",
      "basis_locator": "E14",
      "basis": {
        "type": "reference_evidence",
        "text": "In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers."
      }

The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers."

The beating degree and Water Retention Value (WRV) for the unreﬁned and reﬁned samples:\n(a) softwood ﬁbers and (b) hardwood ﬁbers.\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a\nfunction of the reﬁning revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing\nﬁbrillation and ﬁnes during PFI reﬁning, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood\nﬁber had a more signiﬁcant increase when compared to that of hardwood ﬁber. It is for that ﬁber\nlength plays an essential role in wet–web strength. [24].\nThe above results showed that PFI reﬁning improved the extent of ﬁbrillation (especially the internal\nﬁbrillation), the swelling of ﬁbers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile\nstrength of ﬁbers.\n\nFigure 3. The rheological analysis of wet sheets, the tensile strength of dry sheets, and the ﬁber strength\nfor unreﬁned and reﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁbers and (b) hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n3.2. Eﬀect of PFI Reﬁning on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two ﬁbers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates\nthat the PFI reﬁning is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource\n(Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood ﬁbers showed a reduction\nof 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood ﬁbers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%,\nrespectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than\nthe CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-ﬁtting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of\nCI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated signiﬁcantly for both softwood ﬁbers and\nhardwood ﬁbers, with a correlation coeﬃcient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood ﬁbers and 0.925 (p < 0.05)\nfor hardwood ﬁbers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. FT-IR谱在1016 cm−1处归一化，并用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线，以便从二阶导数谱确定各氢键组分的峰位。 [3]
拟合波段为3000–3700 cm−1，采用Gaussian函数，在Peakfit 4.12软件中进行非线性拟合。 [3]
论文将3000–3700 cm−1的羟基谱带去卷积为四个主要谱带，并依据峰位指认不同氢键类型。 [7]
不同氢键的相对含量按对应拟合谱带的面积比例计算。 [7]
指认的峰位包括O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键约3227 cm−1、O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键约3346 cm−1和O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键约3452 cm−1。 [7]
分析中还讨论了free OH(2)和OH(6)的相对含量变化。 [6]

MinerU章节107块

光谱在1016 cm−1归一化，并用Savitzky–Golay算法获得二阶导数曲线，以确定氢键组分峰位。 [2]
非线性拟合的波段为3000–3700 cm−1的羟基区。 [2] [4]
非线性拟合采用Gaussian函数，并使用Peakfit 4.12软件。 [2]
该羟基区被去卷积为四个主要谱带，峰位用于归属不同氢键；例如约3227 cm−1为O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键、3346 cm−1为O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键、3452 cm−1为O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键。 [4]
不同氢键的相对含量按各去卷积谱带的面积占比计算。 [4]

PyMuPDF 81块归档对照

PyMuPDF结构81块

论文将3000–3700 cm−1的羟基吸收带解卷积为四个主要子峰，并依据各子峰的面积占比分别计算不同氢键的相对含量。 [2] [3]
拟合前光谱在1016 cm−1归一化，并用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线；各氢键组分的峰位取自二阶导数谱，并按不同氢键归属区确定。 [3]
对3000–3700 cm−1区间采用Gaussian函数，在Peakfit 4.12软件中进行非线性拟合。 [3]
各氢键的归属区间为：3580–3550 cm−1对应free OH(2)和OH(6)，3455–3410 cm−1对应O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键，3375–3340 cm−1对应O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键，3310–3230 cm−1对应O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键（cellulose I）。 [6]
文中还给出约3227、3346、3452 cm−1分别对应O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键、O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键和O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键。 [2]

PFI2-020 · 论文说打浆后氢键能量和距离基本不变，那是不是说明打浆对氢键网络基本没影响？

参考答案与必答要点
不表示完全不变。本文三类氢键的峰位几乎不变，因此据公式推得能量和距离基本不变；但相对含量仍变化：0到16000转，针叶木分子间氢键由28.23%变为23.56%，阔叶木由26.55%变为24.98%。应区分单类氢键能量/距离与不同组分的相对分布。

MinerU原生117块

论文的结果是：在PFI打浆全过程中，O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键、O(3)H···O(5)与O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键的峰位几乎保持不变，因而由峰位计算的氢键能量和氢键距离也基本不变。 [1]
但同一研究指出，在氢键距离和能量几乎不变的同时，结晶指数、微晶尺寸以及各类氢键的含量会随打浆发生变化。 [3]
其中，分子间O(6)H···O(3′)氢键的含量与XRD得到的结晶指数显著相关，Pearson相关系数为软木纤维0.888（p < 0.05）、硬木纤维0.889（p < 0.05）。 [3]
因此，不能据此认为打浆对氢键网络基本没影响；更准确的表述是氢键的能量和距离等参数基本稳定，而氢键含量/数量及其与结晶区堆积相关的网络组织发生了改变。 [1] [3]

    "text": "Received: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\nKeywords: natural cellulosic fibers; mechanical refining; Crystallinity; Crystallite size; Hydrogen bonds",

MinerU章节107块

论文报告PFI打浆过程中三种氢键的峰位几乎不变，因此由公式计算得到的氢键能量和氢键距离基本不变。 [1]
摘要明确指出，打浆后晶型、氢键距离和氢键能量几乎不变，而结晶指数、微晶尺寸以及各种氢键的含量随打浆发生变化。 [3]
表2显示氢键相对含量会随打浆改变，例如针叶木纤维的O(6)H···O(3′)氢键从28.23变为23.56，O(3)H···O(5)氢键从28.44变为34.92（16000转）。 [6]
论文结论认为，可及性、润胀和纤丝化的变化与超分子结构密切相关，分子间氢键在纤维素晶体堆叠中起重要作用。 [3]

This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKeywords: natural cellulosic fibers; mechanical refining; Crystallinity; Crystallite size; Hydrogen bonds",

PyMuPDF结构81块

论文观察到软木和硬木纤维中三类氢键的峰位在整个打浆过程中几乎保持不变，因此氢键能量和氢键距离基本不变。 [1]
同一研究的摘要指出，打浆后晶型、氢键距离和各类氢键的能量几乎不变，但结晶指数、微晶尺寸和不同氢键的含量随打浆发生变化。 [7]
所以不能由氢键能量和距离基本不变推出打浆对氢键网络基本没影响；该结果只反映局部氢键参数稳定，而不同氢键的含量和网络组成仍可能改变。 [1] [7]

    "page_start": 10,

    "text": "3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds decreased first and then had an increase, followed by a decline for the two fibers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation coeficients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 $( p < 0 . 0 5 )$ for hardwood fibers, respectively. The similar trends in the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a higher content of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated in Figure 9 [35].",
    "verification": {
      "status": "needs_source_review",
      "exact_other_pages": [],
      "note": "A text extraction mismatch is not automatically a false citation or a zero quality score."
    }
  },
  {
    "ref": "[3]",
    "page_start": 1,
    "page_end": 1,
    "text": "Received: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\nKeywords: natural cellulosic fibers; mechanical refining; Crystallinity; Crystallite size; Hydrogen bonds",
    "verification": {

MinerU原生117块

PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内部分丝（细胞壁分层、松弛和润胀）、外部分丝（从纤维表面剥离但仍附着的微纤丝）、纤维缩短和细小纤维生成。 [1]
这些PFI打浆作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀性、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [1]
随PFI打浆转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著上升，这归因于更高程度的分丝产生新表面和更多孔隙；WRV所反映的润胀使纤维横向更柔顺，有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [2]
纸张抗张强度的提高主要归因于PFI打浆过程中的分丝和细小纤维。 [3]
纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起关键作用，软木浆湿纸幅强度增幅比硬木浆更显著；同时零-span抗张指数显示PFI打浆没有降低纤维强度。 [3]

    "text": "1. Introduction\n\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

MinerU章节107块

PFI打浆的主要作用包括内纤丝化、外纤丝化、纤维切断和细小纤维生成，这些作用提高纤维的可及性、润胀性、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [1]
PFI打浆提高纤丝化程度，尤其内纤丝化，并提高纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，同时不降低纤维抗张强度。 [3]
纸页抗张强度的增量主要归因于PFI打浆过程中的纤丝化和细小纤维。 [3]
湿纸幅强度中纤维长度起关键作用，且softwood纤维的湿纸幅强度增幅比hardwood纤维更显著。 [3]
由WRV表征的润胀增加使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [4]
零-span抗张指数结果表明PFI打浆没有降低纤维强度，因此纸页增强主要来自纤维间结合等结构变化而非单纤维弱化。 [3]
现有证据未给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV对纸页强度的定量贡献排序，因此不能据此判定WRV贡献最大。 [3] [4]

luna：要点83.33%；事实6/7；引用8/8；引用组6/7；边界1/2。

Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

PyMuPDF 81块归档对照

PyMuPDF结构81块

PFI打浆的机械作用首先引起内部细纤维化，即纤维壁分层、松弛和润胀。 [2]
同时发生外部细纤维化，即从纤维表面剥离仍附着的微细纤维，并伴随纤维切断和细小纤维形成。 [2]
这些作用提高纤维的可及性、润胀性、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [2]
随PFI打浆转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著升高，原因是细纤维化产生新表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
WRV升高表示纤维润胀增强，使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
纸页抗张强度的增量主要来自PFI打浆过程中不断增强的细纤维化和细小纤维。 [3]
纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起重要作用，而零距抗张结果表明PFI打浆未降低纤维自身强度。 [3]
文献在讨论强度时把干抗张强度增量主要归因于细纤维化和细小纤维，但没有给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV三者贡献大小的定量排序。 [1] [3]
